confirmedByUser.english: Georgia for all headings, body, navigation and captions
confirmedByUser.chinese: Songti SC / 宋体 for all headings, body, navigation and captions
confirmedByUser.englishWeight: Regular / 400, including Latin runs inside bold Chinese paragraphs

designDefaults.typeScale: v1 design baseline; sizes may be adjusted after real layout review without going below the reading minimum
designDefaults.articleLarge: 18px is an optional unconfirmed exploration, never automatically applied to case-study prose

implementationNotes: px are design reference units. Implement text sizes in rem using the browser default 16px reference; preserve user zoom and text-size preferences.
Breakpoints describe type modes, not a required website framework. Fluid interpolation is optional within the defined endpoints.

2026-11-07 user override: every semantic font stack starts with Georgia for Latin glyphs and falls back to Songti SC for Chinese. Applies to headings, prose, top project menu, side outline, controls and captions. Keep type sizes, weights and ASCII rendering behavior independent.
No font files are bundled by these tokens. Webfont resources and cross-platform fallbacks are resolved during implementation; do not copy system font files into the public site.
The approved existing Songti dot-text interaction stays a separate effect; this file does not replace its font or motion parameters.
Use body.article (alias of body.default) for case-study prose. body.articleLarge is exploratory and must not be substituted automatically.
The local Vite/React app generates CSS from these tokens via scripts/design-tokens.mjs. Keep GitHub publication separate from local development.
English always uses Georgia Regular, including Latin substrings in bold Chinese prose; the local Latin face mapping does not change Chinese weight.

latinRegularFace.note: Bind Latin glyphs to the installed Georgia Regular face even inside bold Chinese text. The declared range prevents synthetic Latin bold; Chinese continues to use its existing Songti weight.
